title: Chapter 44: The Usage of Despair
content:
Chapter 44:

The Usage of Despair

“—You were talking a pretty big game back there, but…”

Fifteen minutes after his declaration of war right in front of the Witchbeast Forest, Ram prefaced her statement with a sidelong glance at Subaru walking beside her.

“Thinking about it calmly, there’s absolutely no condition requiring Barusu to fight on the front lines.”

“Hey, hey, hold on. That’s true, sure, but look at my overflowing motivation. Equipped with this venerable one-handed sword gifted by the village youth group, I am living the fantasy dream right now!”

“And you wouldn’t even have that sword if Lady Beatrice hadn’t stopped you from going completely unarmed, Barusu. Going in empty-handed would have been a one-way ticket to dead-weight status.”

“I honestly can’t deny that.”

Readjusting his grip on the unfamiliar hilt, Subaru dropped his shoulders and let out a sigh.

A black scabbard, a copper-colored hilt, and a blade roughly the length of his arm. Unable to hide his bewilderment at how unexpectedly light it felt, it was a weapon he had acquired following the advice of Beatrice, who had frantically stopped him from charging into the Witchbeast Forest barehanded.

The severity of the situation deepened as time passed. That very sense of urgency was what nearly made him choose to rush in immediately, but looking back calmly, he readily admitted it would have been suicide.

Putting up an unapproachable front while still doing good work when it counted was just part of that drill-haired girl’s difficult nature.

“By the way, can you even use a sword, Barusu?”

“Hard to say, it’s iffy. I do have a second-dan in middle school kendo, but I don’t think real swordsmanship and school kendo can be treated the same way.”

Swinging the sword at his hip back and forth, Subaru replied while feeling its weight.

Three years in middle school, and after that, doing practice swings for no real reason whenever he had free time. Compared to a complete amateur who had never touched one, he figured he could use it somewhat, but he doubted his skill went beyond the level of merely dabbling.

The mismatched one-handed sword was a blade he had received from a young man in the village youth group.

He couldn’t exactly be stupidly honest and tell them, ‘I’m about to go into the Witchbeast Forest,’ so he had managed to get them to hand it over after a rather flimsy excuse, but how useful it would actually be was currently unknown.

And that wasn’t the only thing entrusted to him in the village.

“In my pockets… I’ve got candy, a pretty stone, and—whoa!! There’s a bug in here!”

Rummaging through his pockets stuffed with various things, Subaru let out a yelp at a nasty sensation. The winged insect, having been trapped in a cramped space, left his hand and disappeared straight into the depths of the forest. Watching it go, Subaru pantomimed wiping his forehead and said,

“Taking advantage of the chaos, what a bunch of ridiculous brats. I’m going to lecture them later.”

“It’s proof that they adore you… Whatever do they see in a man like this?”

“To the innocent eyes of a child, the true essence of the man known as me shines through brilliantly.”

As Ram looked at him with unamused eyes, looking as though she might scoff at any moment, Subaru wagged his head from side to side, pointed a finger at her, and said, “A-nd a-l-s-o,”

“This time, it’s not just for me; it includes their thanks to Rem, too. If anything, I’m just the delivery boy bringing it to her. You get it now? Just watch.”

“…Ram supposes.”

Hearing Ram’s voice, which seemed hesitant to agree, Subaru nodded repeatedly with a satisfied look.

The interaction before leaving the village had struck a chord with Subaru in its own way. He hoped it had been the same for Ram, who had been watching it unfold just like him.

—Leaving the village and entering the Witchbeast Forest.

The ones who noticed Subaru and the others trying to sneak into the forest behind the villagers’ backs were the children, who were still suffering the lingering effects of having their mana drained.

Wanting to thank Subaru and Rem directly, they spotted Subaru’s group and, claiming it was a token of their gratitude, shoved all sorts of things into his pockets.

The candy, the pretty stone, and even that winged insect were all physical manifestations of their gratitude. There was no way he could treat them carelessly. Even though the bug had flown away.

And so, to a flustered Subaru who had been burdened with rather unnecessary forms of thanks, the children smiled and said:

“‘We want to say thank you to Rem-rin too, so bring her back later, okay…’ Huh.”

Just how dangerous a place she was in right now, and what she was putting her life on the line to fight for.

The children didn’t know. And they didn’t need to know.

Because—

“Don’t worry, you little brats. I’m going to lecture you troublemakers who wandered into the dark forest at night right alongside your big sister who did something rash without even consulting me.”

He could probably add to that list a reckless idiot boy who went into the forest, got bitten all over by dogs, and caused a massive nuisance to everyone around him.

Spending the whole night sitting in seiza and getting chewed out by the village chief wouldn’t be half bad either.

Naturally, his lips broke into a grin at the vision of the future he had drawn up.

However, seeing Subaru smirking faintly like that,

“Regardless, you are walking too slowly, Barusu.”

Ram, looking back at him from far ahead with an exasperated expression, stated as much.

Marching briskly onward, Ram traversed the supposedly treacherous footing of the forest with ease. Despite wearing her usual maid outfit, her pace was no different than if she were crossing the mansion’s courtyard.

Meanwhile, Subaru…

“G-Give me a break, would you? I’m running low on blood, and also guts. Oh, right, I missed my chance to have Emilia-tan tell me to have a safe trip!”

“You haven’t said ‘I’m home’ yet, so last night’s ‘Have a safe trip’ is still valid.”

“I-Is that how it works…?”

Struggling with a swaying body and a spinning head, he tottered forward, using the one-handed sword as a walking stick.

His march couldn’t be called fast even as a compliment, and as things stood, he was only feeding the impatience of Ram, who was walking ahead.

Unlike last night, this search through the forest was taking place with the sun high in the sky. Visibility was vastly clearer compared to after sunset, but the thick, overgrown foliage still made it hard to see far ahead.

He thought they were walking through the same sort of areas as last night, but he couldn’t deny the possibility that they were heading in completely the wrong direction. The sheer depth of the forest seemed to warp the directional sense of anyone who entered it; he genuinely believed that if he were alone, he wouldn’t even be able to find the exit and would have wound up hopelessly lost.

“Wait a moment again, Barusu. —Clairvoyance, awaken.”

Stopping him with her hand, Ram muttered those words, and her right eye dyed a deep crimson.

Ever since they entered the forest, Ram had been periodically using her Clairvoyance, searching for any sign of Rem, who was supposed to be in there. But unfortunately, it had yet to yield any results.

Was she outside the range of Ram’s vision, or perhaps—

“Stop thinking about the worst-case scenario. Fate-sama will just gleefully swoop in to make it a reality…”

Smacking himself on the head, he buried the terrible outcome that had drifted into his mind.

Three or four hours had already passed since Rem deceived her sister and the villagers to enter the forest. Compared to them, who were pursuing her on a delay, it was impossible to even fathom just how deep into the woods she had gone. However, considering the sheer scale of her objective, even running from one corner of the forest to the other wouldn’t be enough.

It brought to mind once again exactly what Rem was trying to do, and the incredibly high difficulty of Subaru’s own survival.

Even understanding all that, he was utterly exasperated by his own sense of self-preservation that was making it so hard for him to take the plunge.

“Ah, how pathetic. Focus, I need to focus. Dedicate yourself to guarding defenseless Ram while she’s using Clairvoyance, and don’t think about anything unnecessary.”

Drawing the one-handed sword from its scabbard, he lightly sliced through the air to check its feel.

The sound of it parting the air was quiet, and its weight was somewhat lighter even when compared to a bokken. The length of the blade made this one easier to handle; the only thing left was purely whether or not he had the resolve to wield a live blade.

“They say in actual combat, just getting the blade angle right on a real sword is a pain, too.”

When an amateur wields a blade, it wobbles, meaning they fundamentally can't cut through things straight.

He swung the blade up at a thin tree branch directly in front of him, letting off a flash with an upward slash from directly below—the branch, about as thick as Subaru’s wrist, was effortlessly severed and spun to the ground.

He involuntarily let out an “Ooh,” highly praising his own handiwork. Leaking a sigh of admiration at the lack of resistance that went beyond his expectations, Subaru continued his sword dance.

One strike, two strikes; every time he swung, branches and leaves scattered as the ferocity of his slashes increased.

Reconfirming the fact that his three years in middle school and his subsequent life of practice swings were surprisingly paying off, he got carried away and performed a massive horizontal sweep with the blade—

“Ah.”

With a sharp thwack, the blade buried itself halfway into the thick trunk of a tree.

Easy to enter, hard to escape. The embedded blade wouldn’t budge no matter what he did. Sweating profusely on the inside, Subaru looked back at Ram, confirmed that she was still sharing vision via Clairvoyance, and then desperately planted his foot against the trunk and struggled to pull the sword out.

“Crap crap crap, this is so uncool! Losing my sword like this is totally lame! Come off, pull out, at worst it’s fine if you break in half, just come out…”

“—Barusu, something is looking this way.”

Behind Subaru, who was still fighting to dislodge the stuck sword, Ram, who had lost her immediate line of sight due to her Clairvoyance, shouted.

—Something was looking this way. Subaru shuddered at her warning. If she, who could share the vision of others, was announcing that, it meant the entity was…

“Within visual range of us…!”

Letting go of the stubborn hilt, Subaru frantically looked around. Then, to his left—leaping across the tree branches, a shadow was closing in on them at a terrifying speed.

Registering that it was the quadrupedal beast he was already thoroughly sick of seeing, Subaru immediately abandoned the task of yanking out the sword. Crouching down, he picked up a few reasonably sized stones and—

“No time to pull out the Holy Sword, so eat this!!”

He pitched a fist-sized stone with all his might at the shadow soaring through the air. The spinning chunk packed enough power to instantly incapacitate if it scored a direct hit, but unfortunately, it was an amateur’s throw. Not to mention, with the target moving, whether it hit or not was strictly in the realm of miracles.

His rapid-fire throws proved useless; every single stone vanished into the depths of the forest. As if mocking Subaru’s clumsy resistance, the witchbeast bent a branch and launched itself into an exceptionally sharp glide—landing on the ground and lowering its posture just a few paces away from Subaru. But,

“Alright, step right up!!”

As if to say he had completely read its movements, he unleashed a full swing resembling an uppercut.

The strike aimed at the landed witchbeast’s face utilized the emptied, iron-fitted scabbard as his weapon of choice. It was a perfectly timed move, predicting that if his stone-throwing feints missed, the beast would attack like this. He would smash the witchbeast’s snout with the thick hilt-side of the scabbard—or so he had planned.

“Hah?!”

A tremendous whooshing sound echoed as he completely whiffed, and stepping on dead grass, Subaru’s footing slipped spectacularly.

At the moment of impact, the witchbeast had further lowered its posture while charging, slightly shifting the point of contact. Thus, the scabbard only managed to graze the fur on the witchbeast’s back. Conversely, Subaru, having let loose the widest of wide swings, left his back completely unguarded, resulting in the twisting witchbeast’s fangs having an impossibly wide opening to strike.

Right behind him, the presence of the witchbeast turning around, gouging the earth, and bearing its fangs. Feeling a chill down his nape, he just barely tilted his neck—just before those sharp canines could tear into his calf,

“What are you playing around for at a crucial moment like this?”

A violent gust of wind caught the leaping witchbeast, wildly disrupting its midair movement and throwing off its aim.

Failing to brace itself from the unexpected intervention, the witchbeast crashed. It rolled on the ground and immediately tried to stand up, but its four limbs merely trembled violently as it sprawled there, completely paralyzed.

Regripping his scabbard, Subaru stared in agitation at the immobilized witchbeast, its breathing ragged. Raising the scabbard so he could strike down at any moment, he sidestepped his way over to Ram.

Ram, her palm aimed at the crouching witchbeast, saw Subaru line up beside her and let out a scoffing “Hmph,”

“Your armament has gotten quite shabby in just a short amount of time.”

“I fully admit both my drop in attack power and my own blunder. So, what’s its status?”

He pointed at the unmoving witchbeast, questioning Ram, who was presumably the one doing it. The witchbeast had already closed its eyes and wasn’t twitching a muscle, almost as if it had fallen asleep.

Confirming this, Ram gently lowered the palm she had directed at the witchbeast and said,

“It’s finished.”

“Huh?”

“Ram stopped its breathing, is what she said.”

Surprised by Ram declaring it so nonchalantly, Subaru approached the witchbeast half in doubt. Poking the body that only looked asleep with the tip of his scabbard and getting no reaction, he boldly flipped it over. Its four limbs sprawled limply, its tongue lolling out of its mouth; there was no sign of life. It was, indeed, dead.

“What did you, do to make it like this?”

“Ram told you, didn’t she? That she can use wind magic a little. Ram severed the tendons in its limbs with a blade of wind and crushed its throat to suffocate it, that’s all. —Ram has no intention of letting it suffer needlessly.”

Ram spoke as if it were nothing. Looking closely, a faint trail of blood was indeed dripping from the extremities of the witchbeast’s limbs, and an agony akin to gasping for air could be seen on its face.

Confirming these details, Subaru couldn’t suppress a variety of questions bubbling up towards Ram. Such as, how exactly does this qualify as ‘can use wind magic a little’, or that it lacked the flashiness you’d expect from magic, or that it just made her look exactly like an assassin.

However, it seemed Subaru wasn’t the only one wanting to retort to their partner.

Before Subaru could even sort through the numerous candidates that popped into his head, Ram gazed at the one-handed sword still stuck halfway into the tree trunk,

“Useless.”

“Guh…”

That blunt expression, requiring no further elaboration, pierced him the deepest.

As Subaru clutched his chest and dropped to his knees, Ram gave a small shrug and walked over to the trunk where the sword was embedded. Then, pointing her palm at the wood, she used another blade of wind to gouge out the trunk’s surface, effortlessly succeeding in liberating the sword. Though looking sullen, Subaru frantically rushed to catch the sword Ram picked up and tossed at him,

“Thanks, but can we not throw a naked blade end-over-end at someone?!”

Giving up on catching it, he retrieved the sword that had impaled the ground. Wiping off the dirt, he returned it to the scabbard, thinking somewhat lame jokes to himself about how they were ‘back in the scabbard’ together. Suddenly, Ram tilted her head,

“Still, that ulgarm just now bypassed a defenseless Ram and went for you instead, Barusu. Just like last night, it seems you’re quite popular with them.”

“Ah, yeah. My phero-moans are really acting up, after all.”

Putting his hands together lightly towards the witchbeast’s corpse in prayer, Subaru then scratched his neck while vaguely confirming Ram’s observation.

The sensation of being prioritized as a target by the witchbeasts had indeed continued since last night. As these results piled up, Subaru’s hypothesis was drawing closer to conviction.

In any case,

“So, did you spot Rem with that Clairvoyance earlier?”

“No, unfortunately. It’s possible she’s even deeper into the forest. We’d better hurry… Though that will exponentially increase the chances of you being attacked, Barusu.”

Glancing sideways at Subaru, Ram touched her pale cheek as if pondering something.

Her gaze shifted back and forth between Subaru and the witchbeast, before she nodded, seemingly having reached a vague conclusion.

“Ram knew it, it’s because you look weak.”

“That’s the conclusion you puzzled over? How rude.”

“Then, it’s because you look like an easy mark.”

“The fundamental part hasn’t changed at all, onee-sama.”

“Standing around talking won’t improve the situation. Let’s find Rem.”

“…Y-Yeah, you’re right.”

With a partner who refused to break her own pace no matter what, Subaru found it somewhat hard to work with her. Pretending not to notice his inner thoughts, she headed deeper into the forest.

Chasing after her back, Subaru suddenly voiced something that had been bothering him.

“Can I ask what ‘hornless’ is?”

It was a word Ram herself had uttered before they entered the forest.

It was a word he could somewhat guess the meaning of. In response, Ram did not stop walking, nor did she look back as she answered,

“It is exactly as it sounds: a derogatory term for a fool who lost their horn despite being an Oni.”

At the appearance of the word ‘Oni,’ the scene from last night resurfaced in Subaru’s mind.

Deep in the forest, Rem laughing uproariously, bathed in splattered blood. The white horn sharply protruding from her forehead was unforgettable. It was truly the exact image of an oni straight out of a fairy tale.

However, there was no sign whatsoever of a horn on the forehead of Ram, who was supposed to be her twin. Of course, it might be hidden beneath the white brim indispensable to her maid attire, but that possibility had just been rejected by her own mouth a moment ago.

Perhaps sensing Subaru’s silent lack of comprehension, Ram slid her hand into her pink hair and said,

“Due to a minor dispute, Ram lost the only horn she had. Ever since then, she had relied on Rem for everything.”

“…Ah, did I ask something I shouldn’t have?”

“Why?”

Walking ahead, Ram turned around and tilted her head, genuinely perplexed. In response, Subaru scratched his cheek as he answered,

“Well, I don’t know how big a deal a horn is to the Oni race, but my guess is it’s a pretty massive issue. And I figured I might’ve pried into it pretty rudely.”

“If that were so, it'd be far too late to bring up after you already went and dug it up. —But, rest assured.”

After intimidating Subaru by lowering her voice a fraction, Ram softened her expression slightly,

“Whatever the case back then, Ram is at peace with it now. Through losing her horn, there are things she gained and lives that were saved. It’s all just part of fate.”

Quite magnanimous of her, Subaru thought to himself.

However, after stating that, Ram cast a shadow over her expression, prefacing with a “But,”

“Rem likely does not think that way. —Which is exactly why Ram has to find her quickly.”

Facing forward again, Ram gave him a hand signal to stop.

It was time for Clairvoyance. Making sure not to screw it up this time, he stayed on high alert around her.

Her right eye dyed deep crimson, and her vision shifted from here to far beyond. At the destination of her leaping vision, she would jump into yet another field of view, searching out her intended target.

Borrowing the vision of a creature with a matching wavelength. Subaru didn’t know how that act made the world look, nor did he know just how much of a burden it placed on the caster, and he didn’t ask.

Every time she used Clairvoyance, tears of blood streamed down Ram’s pale cheek. Both her legs trembled minutely, as if she had been walking for a full day, and her body, which stubbornly kept moving forward, swayed repeatedly as if struck by vertigo. Even so, Ram refused to stop her advance through the forest.

Subaru felt that he couldn’t just leave things to Ram, who never once uttered a word about how painful or agonizing it was.

Down to their very core, the twins, she and Rem, were ultimately two of a kind. The type of nature that wouldn’t hesitate to take on the burden, so long as it was them pushing themselves too far.

Including Emilia, the women of that manor were just a bit too prone to prioritizing others over themselves.

“You should all just look down at your own feet and panic more, like me. —You’re making me hate myself for being so completely pathetic in comparison.”

He kicked the grass at his feet. A massive miscalculation; the scattered grass flew into his mouth, and kicked-up dirt got in his eyes. Hurriedly spitting “Peh, peh,” he felt incredibly awkward about his own lack of cool.

But realizing that kind of buffoonery suited him perfectly, Subaru felt the illusion that his somewhat stiffened heart had lightened just a little.

That’s why,

“Ram, is Rem precious to you? Are you worried about her?”

A question asked despite knowing it was bad to disturb her focus while she was using Clairvoyance.

Her eye bloodshot, her vision placed far from here, Ram answered a beat late,

“Obviously. It’s true that she is stronger than Ram. But that doesn’t mean Ram shouldn’t worry about her.”

“…Yeah.”

“Even if she’s vastly superior to Ram in everything she does, Ram is her older sister. That position alone is absolutely unshakable.”

Backed by resolute determination, her position as an older sister was being exercised.

Until learning it anew like this, Subaru had to admit the fact that he had severely misjudged her, thinking she just used that position to act high and mighty.

And now that he had admitted that, Subaru had no choice but to steel his own resolve.

“Truth be told, ideally I would’ve wanted to do this after meeting up with Rem, but oh well.”

Scratching his head, he said that and began doing stretching exercises.

Perhaps sensing something baffling in Subaru’s attitude, Ram, having obtained no results, ended her Clairvoyance and retrieved her vision.

Wiping her blood-pooled right eye with a cloth taken from her breast pocket, she knit her brows suspiciously,

“Barusu, what are you intending to do?”

“In my current state, it’s like I only came along to drag you down. I’m pretty sure I told you before we entered the forest. That I’d actually be useful in saving Rem.”

Though the possibility had only been a fifty-fifty bet, the odds had now recovered to about seventy-thirty in their favor. Naturally, there was the anxiety of his real-life luck drawing that remaining thirty percent, but—

“Seventy-thirty. It’s rare for me to be on the side with the higher win rate. Like hell I’d throw that away. —Ram, are you willing to cross a slightly dangerous bridge?”

“Alone in a forest with starving beasts and a young man—as a maiden, there are few situations more dangerous than this.”

“She’s got some nerve, this big sister.”

He laughed, and then Subaru took a deep breath, opening his eyes wide.

If Subaru’s hypothesis was correct, this should change the situation. Even knowing it was necessary, he couldn’t stop his heart from recoiling in fear.

—There was no stopping the fear now. Being a timid coward was an established fact. Whining and dragging his feet out of fear didn’t matter, so long as he actually put it into practice.

Striking himself with a reprimand that was hard to tell whether it was weak or strong, Subaru voiced it out loud.

If Subaru was right, it would come.

“Ram, the truth is, I—”

—Return by Death,

 he was about to say.

Subaru acted to confess that which he was forbidden to tell, to break the Taboo. Bracing herself for whatever Subaru was about to utter, Ram’s expression froze.

No—time itself had halted.

The world lost its color, sound vanished, and the very concept of time was blown away by the roots.

And in that world where an equal stagnation was imposed upon everything, the solitary entity that escaped that restriction suddenly appeared right before Subaru’s eyes.

“—So you’re here.”

The murmur did not actually form a sound.

But he packed it with all the venom and prayer he could muster, hoping it would reach the thing in front of him. If it understood his feelings even a little, it would lower his frustration considerably.

—In a world where time had frozen, the only thing unaffected by it: the black haze.

Appearing out of nowhere, it began to form the outline of an arm in front of the posturing Subaru. Fingers were born, a wrist sprouted, an elbow grew, and an upper arm extended—up until that point, it was the same mutation of the haze he had witnessed previously. But this time, the third time, there was a further change.

“Up to the shoulder…”

Past the upper arm, a shape resembling a shoulder was modeled.

Having generated everything from the tips of the fingers up to the shoulder, it was now completely fitting to call it a magnificent ‘single arm.’

It had slowly begun to form a clearer image since the first time he saw it. While terrified that the haze’s erosion was progressing with every occurrence, Subaru was given no time to closely ruminate on it.

Into the chest of Subaru, who found the growth of the black haze eerie, the fingers slipped without hesitation.

Slipping right past the thin flesh of his chest, stroking his ribs, making a beeline straight for the heart protected within that sternum.

Even knowing it was coming, pain was not something that could be endured once it crossed a certain threshold.

The pain of having one’s heart directly crushed existed in a realm that couldn’t possibly be articulated without screaming and writhing around like a madman.

A long, agonizing, unbearable time of torment continued.

The rhythm of his heart went mad, blood flow was violently forced out, and his entire body screamed. The pain made bloody tears erupt, and the molars he gritted shattered involuntarily.

Enduring a pain so great that it wouldn’t be strange for all of that to happen, the paralyzed Subaru couldn’t even vent it through outward reactions, leaving him no choice but to continuously absorb it.

Eventually, the time of torment drifted further away, his vision fading to pure white—

“—Barusu?”

Called out to, Subaru realized he had fallen to his knees.

Drool was dribbling from his downcast mouth, and hurriedly wiping it away with his sleeve as he stood up, he said,

“Close one, close one. Just a daydream.”

“You are also still recovering from an illness, Barusu. Do not push yourself, and leave this to Ram. So, what is it we must do to—”

Mid-sentence, Ram’s expression shifted sharply, and she looked around.

Within the forest where silence had fallen, tree branches swayed in the wind, and only the faint rustling of leaves rubbing against each other echoed. Straining her ears to listen, Ram looked at Subaru,

“What did you do, Barusu?”

“…I just tried making a little bet that came with some pain.”

All of that torment, yet not a single trace of it remained anywhere on his body now.

While he found the method of leaving scars exclusively and thoroughly upon the mind to be repulsive, he offered a sliver of gratitude just for the fact that it left him with the physical strength to move.

After all—

“The wind is disturbed… the stench of beasts is approaching. And in tremendous numbers.”

Amidst the deep green that was rustling and beginning to lose its silence, Ram’s face abruptly locked onto the right side. Drawn in, he cast his gaze in the same direction and saw multiple red points of light approaching from the distance.

First came five. Turning to face what they would encounter in roughly a dozen seconds was Ram. Beside her, drawing his one-handed sword from its scabbard, Subaru also prepared for the unavoidable battle.

“We haven’t even found Rem yet…!”

“Well, don’t worry about it. We’ll probably be able to meet up with her before too long.”

“How can you be so certain?”

Shrugging at Ram, who was intimidating him with her sharp glare,

“Rem’s objective is to hunt down every last witchbeast in the forest. —As long as I’m here, those guys are going to take the bait and flock toward me as their prey. So sooner or later, Rem won’t have a choice but to come here too.”

He had been thinking about it all along. He had always wondered.

The reason why the witchbeasts chose Subaru as their target.

Throughout these repeated loops, every time Subaru encountered the witchbeasts, he would invariably be cursed. Rather than it being an unavoidable fate, it was because some sort of compelling force was at work, dictating that whenever they met a witchbeast, Subaru would invariably be selected as the target.

The witchbeasts overreacted to Subaru’s presence. The answer to why could be deduced from the statement of someone else who had overreacted in the exact same way. Namely:

“The Witch’s scent.”

Witchbeasts were the natural enemies of humanity, supposedly created by the Witch.

And they had constantly displayed an excessive reaction towards Subaru, who reeked of the Witch’s stench. It was likely the exact same reason why Subaru had been attacked at every turn since entering the forest.

If the faintly drifting scent was enough to lure out the witchbeasts, then he might as well reek of it magnificently.

So magnificently that every witchbeast in the forest—every single one of them that had placed a curse on Subaru’s body—would gather, bringing even the pursuing Rem right to him.

That was the brilliant plan Subaru had devised to both reunite with Rem and ensure his own survival.

—Dubbed: “Operation Natsuki Subaru, the Great Decoy.”

As always, it was a fighting style that didn’t put him on the very front lines, but the scheme had gone off without a hitch.

He had been helped by catching onto the words Beatrice had muttered back when the haze appeared the one time he had tried to tell Emilia about Return by Death.

With the appearance of the haze, the Witch’s scent enveloping Subaru grew thicker.

—Most likely, that haze had some sort of connection to the Witch.

Therefore, every time the haze appeared, the aura of the Witch drifting from Subaru intensified, ultimately unleashing its effect as live bait to attract the witchbeasts.

An agony he could convey to no one, and an excruciating pain he could confess to no one.

At the exhilaration of taking the fate that had prepared those things and turning it on its head, Subaru twisted the corners of his mouth into a grin, completely leaving behind even the threat closing in before his eyes.

—Ah, I’ve finally managed to strike a blow against the fate that orchestrated this loop!

Cheering in his heart, he regripped his one-handed sword and readied himself against the approaching witchbeasts.

And then, he declared loudly to Ram standing beside him.

“Alright then, I’m fully relying on you for the actual fighting, so I’m in your hands!”

“Objectively reflect on what you're saying later.”

Trailing just behind Ram’s sigh-mingled voice, blades of wind smashed into the pack rushing at them head-on.

—The hostilities with the witchbeasts were about to begin anew, this time with a change in cast.
